66: classical canonical construction on a compact oriented spin three-manifold
67: (or compact support), not an axiom derivation or quantum constraint theorem.
68: Use a three-torus to avoid bundle and boundary qualifications in the native
69: comparison. Fields are smooth, g is positive definite, and there is one
70: complex two-component spinor of each chirality. The equations below also
71: make sense for a single such classical spinor. Quantum interpretation,
72: canonical geometry, the source action and constraint interpretation are
73: supplied. No empirical constants are inferred. Brackets are identities of
74: smooth local functionals with the stated integrations by parts; no global
75: well-posedness theorem for the nonlinear evolution is asserted. Spatial
76: transformations use the identity component with a chosen spin lift, so the
77: fixed spin structure and its possible double cover are respected. Lapses
78: in the bracket identities are smooth real smearings; the spacetime action
79: reconstruction uses N>0. Boundary contributions are excluded by the closed
80: slice or compact-support hypothesis.

82: ## The phase-space term that moving geometry adds
83: 
84: Write a coordinate-row orthonormal inverse frame B, so g=(BB^T)^-1.
85: Rotating B to B R acts on its spinor as psi -> Spin(R)^-1 psi. On the
86: bundle of frames over positive metrics define the matrix connection
87: 
88:     A_B(delta B)=anti(B^-1 delta B),   anti(X)=(X-X^T)/2,
89:     rho(Omega)=Omega_ab sigma_a sigma_b/4.
90: 
91: It transforms as A_(BR)=R^-1 A_B R+R^-1 delta R. Thus delta psi+rho(A)psi
92: is covariant, and i/2 psi^dagger <->(delta+rho(A)) psi is invariant and
93: horizontal under simultaneous frame/spin rotation. At a fixed background
94: coordinate change J independent of the metric variation, B -> J B leaves
95: B^-1 delta B unchanged. This is the appropriate configuration-space
96: connection; it is not the intrinsic spatial Levi-Civita connection.
97: 
98: In the symmetric positive section E=g^-1/2, the reduced symplectic potential is
99: 
100:     Theta = int pi^ij delta g_ij
101:           + i/2 int psi^dagger <->delta psi
102:           + i int psi^dagger rho(A_E(delta E)) psi.          (P1)
103: 
104: Here pi is the gravitational momentum. Its coordinate canonical momentum
105: is P=pi+a, where a(delta g)=i psi^dagger rho(A(delta g)) psi. This is an
106: explicit Darboux description, so nondegeneracy and the Jacobi identity
107: follow from the ordinary product canonical structure. Use {g_ij,P^kl}=
108: delta_(i^k delta_j)^l and {psi_alpha(x),psi_beta^dagger(y)}=-i delta_alpha beta
109:  delta(x-y). For metric coordinates q^I (the six independent components),
110: 
111:     {pi_I,psi}=rho(A_I)psi,
112:     {pi_I,pi_J}=i psi^dagger rho(F_IJ)psi,
113:     F_IJ=partial_I A_J-partial_J A_I+[A_I,A_J].              (P2)
114: 
115: These formulas follow by substituting pi=P-i psi^dagger rho(A)psi.
116: A product bracket for (g,pi,psi) defines a different declared model unless
117: the Hamiltonian and generators are transformed along with the momenta.
118: 
119: For E=I+S, A=-[S,delta S]/2+O(S^2 delta S). Therefore

251:        +2 alpha beta [(d-1)lambda-1] int a^j nabla_j pi.   (P11)
252: 
253: Here a^i=g^ij(N partial_j M-M partial_j N), and the derivative of the
254: density is its density-covariant derivative. The coefficient follows from
255: (pi_ij-lambda pi g_ij)(Hess^ij N-g^ij Delta N)
256: =pi_ij Hess^ij N+[(d-1)lambda-1]pi Delta N.
257: 
258: Strong equality to D_g^can[a] for every field in this ansatz gives
259: 
260:     alpha beta=-1,  lambda=1/(d-1),  gamma arbitrary.       (P12)
261: 
262: These conditions are sufficient by P11. Necessity does not presume that
263: the two structures are independent: at g=I on a torus, use N=1,M=cos x1.
264: A momentum with only pi^22=cos x1 has zero divergence but a nonzero integral
265: of a.partial pi, forcing the second coefficient to vanish. Then only
266: pi^11=cos x1 fixes -alpha beta=1. Thus neither alpha nor beta is zero.
267: The degenerate cases with one zero have zero pure normal bracket and do
268: not satisfy the displayed nonzero strong target for all momenta. This is
269: an ansatz classification, not a classification of every gravitational law.
270: 
271: For d=3, the inverse kinetic trace coefficient is lambda=1/2. Its Legendre
272: inverse has the familiar covariant kinetic trace coefficient 1; these are
273: different coefficients and should not be compared as equal numbers.
274: 
275: ## Full classical closure in this declared family
276: 
277: Use P1/P2, d=3 and H[N]=H_g[N]+H_m[N]. The configuration-curvature addition
278: to {H_g[N],H_g[M]} is zero: both momentum gradients at the same point are
279: the same vector times N or M, and F is antisymmetric. The connection-
280: covariant mixed bracket vanishes after antisymmetrization in N,M by P5:
281: each factor is ultralocal in its lapse. Thus P11 and P9 give, at P12,
282: 
283:     {H[N],H[M]}=D_total[g^-1(N dM-M dN)],
284:     {D_total[a],H[N]}=H[L_a N],
285:     {D_total[a],D_total[b]}=D_total[[a,b]].                (P13)
286: 
287: The latter two follow from the invariant symplectic potential, scalar
288: Hamiltonian density and equivariant spatial action. This is strong
289: classical closure on the stated smooth phase space. It is not an
290: operator-ordered quantum algebra or a proof of its anomaly cancellation.
291: Necessity of P12 for this combined ansatz follows already on psi=0.
292: The coefficient gamma and nonzero alpha remain free; this construction
293: alone supplies no value for Newton's constant or the cosmological term.
294: 
295: The metric equation is dot g-L_shift g=2N alpha(pi_ij-pi g_ij/2)/sqrt(g).
296: Writing K_ij=(dot g-L_shift g)_ij/(2N), Legendre inversion gives
297: pi^ij=sqrt(g)(K^ij-Kg^ij)/alpha and the metric Lagrangian
298: 
299:     L_g=N sqrt(g)/alpha [K_ij K^ij-K^2+R-alpha gamma].      (P14)
300: 
301: Hence it is the ADM Einstein-Hilbert family with 16 pi G=alpha and
302: 2 Lambda=alpha gamma, provided those conventional identifications are
303: chosen. A healthy TT kinetic branch asks alpha>0; that sign is an added
304: physical requirement, not selected by the algebra. Matter contributes the
305: last term of P1 to the Lagrangian and the H_m/D_m source terms. Dropping
306: that term changes the canonical structure used to establish P13.
307:
